narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s an **80% chance** you may not pass your final year. This is far above the 10% threshold that triggers the requirement for remedial courses—meaning the system is strongly advising extra support to help you succeed.

The decision isn’t random; it’s based on three key factors that stood out the most. The strongest signal is your **history of past academic struggles**, which is far above what’s typical for students who don’t need extra help. While most students have never failed a class before, you’ve had at least one failure, making it harder to catch up without targeted assistance.

Another major influence is your **family’s educational background**. Both your mother and father have only completed primary education, which is less common among students who pass without intervention—only about 7% of them share this background. When parents haven’t pursued higher education themselves, students often face additional challenges accessing resources or encouragement to excel academically.

The third factor, while less impactful, is actually a positive one: your **clear goal of pursuing higher education**. Unlike some students who may not have long-term academic ambitions, your determination to continue studying works in your favor. However, it’s not enough on its own to override the other risks.

To improve your chances, focus on **reducing absences**—you’ve missed nearly three times as many classes as the average student who passes—and consider increasing your **weekly study time**, which is currently below what most successful students dedicate. Remedial courses are designed to give you the extra tools you need, so take advantage of them. With effort and support, you can turn this prediction around.
